# RETRO: PR #12245

## What worked

- Cross-examination was decisive. Sol's independent final missed F1 (the lockView id-scope blocker) and F2 (FALLBACK, where it read Hyprland 0.51.1). A neutral mechanism-only follow-up had Sol confirm both from source at the installed version.
- Opus's follow-up turned Sol's sleep-monitor race into a mocked demonstration with the real script. It also surfaced a new SIGTERM hang.
- The non-GUI `qml6 --apptype core` analog with a positive control gave runtime evidence for F1 without a compositor.

## Process deviations

- **Opus dispatch:** first-call rules were only in `brief.md`, not in the dispatch text. The coordinator runtime section prescribes the exact one-line prompt, which conflicts with the PR13009 correction. Suggest updating the runtime section so the prescribed prompt starts with the first-call rules.
- **Opus GUI processes:** Opus started GUI-mode `qml6` and `quickshell` processes inside `review.py`, contrary to the brief: two offscreen `qml6` runs, four `quickshell` launches and one `qml6 --help`, which aborted with exit 134 and core dumps off. The bundle is excluded and no conclusions rely on it.
- **Opus host syntax check:** Opus ran `bash -n` on its own fixture script on the host, outside `review.py`. No PR code was involved.
- **Opus disk use:** the Opus run bundles snapshot full source trees, about 1.1 GB under `opus/plans/`. The follow-up runs were scoped to about 200 KB. Suggest review.py fixtures default to minimal snapshots.
- **Sol read bound:** one 90-line read in the follow-up, above the 50-line bound.
- **Opus cleanup incident:** the first `sleeprace` run timed out because its cleanup hit the SIGTERM bug. The run is preserved, and the corrected run was used.

## Improvements

- The brief should name the exact installed dependency versions, or ask reviewers to probe them first. Sol's final used older Hyprland and systemd sources.
- Grep-only QML tests are a recurring blind spot. A small reusable non-GUI QML harness for Service logic would help reviewers.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** At head `2c1db6d`, password unlock fails on every submit: the new focus helper throws before PAM starts, so only fingerprint unlock still works. A second change can drop a lock requested while no physical display is connected. Several other parts work as described (see **Verified** below).

### Password submits throw before PAM starts

`forceLockPasswordFocus()` (`shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml:79-83`) reads the id `lockView`. That id is declared inside the `WlSessionLockSurface` (`Service.qml:431`), which Quickshell 0.3.1 takes as a `QQmlComponent*` default property. A component gets its own id scope, so `lockView` is not visible from `Service`'s functions, and the read throws `ReferenceError: lockView is not defined`.

```text
LockView onAccepted: clears the field, calls root.submitPassword(pw)
└─ submitPassword()                  Service.qml:326
   └─ runWake()                      called first, Service.qml:330
      └─ forceLockPasswordFocus()    new last line of runWake
         └─ reads lockView  →  ReferenceError, submitPassword() stops here
            (never reached: pendingPassword, authenticatingPassword = true, passwordPam.start())
```

**Impact:** The typed password disappears with no "Checking…" and no failure message, and PAM never runs. Fingerprint unlock is unaffected. Without an enrolled fingerprint, recovery needs a TTY. The same exception fires on every wake event and screen change, so the intended focus restoration (#7811) never runs either.

A non-GUI Qt 6.11.2 analog with the same component boundary threw this `ReferenceError`. The same code without the boundary completed. Not reproduced on a real lock screen.

**Suggested change:** Do not reach into the surface component by id. For example, expose a counter or signal on `Service` that each `LockView` observes and answers by calling its own `forcePasswordFocus()`. A `typeof lockView` guard would only turn this into a silent no-op.

### A lock requested with no physical display is dropped after 15 s

`realScreenCount()` now skips screens named `FALLBACK` (`Service.qml:60-75`). In Hyprland 0.56.2, `FALLBACK` is a real headless `wl_output` that the compositor creates when the last monitor is removed (`src/state/FallbackState.cpp`, `src/managers/ProtocolManager.cpp`). It is not a Quickshell placeholder: Quickshell filters placeholders by `isPlaceholder()`, not by name.

| Lock requested while only `FALLBACK` exists | Merge-base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Lock target | locks on `FALLBACK` | stays pending (no real screen) |
| After 15 s | still locked | `clearStalledLockRequest()` sets `lockRequested = false` |
| Physical display returns later | lock surface appears | `requestSessionLock()` returns at `!lockRequested`: desktop unlocked |

**Impact:** Examples include a desktop whose only monitor drops hot-plug detect when switched off before the idle lock, or a KVM switched to another machine. `lock()` returned `"ok"` when the request was made. The only trace of the dropped lock is the log line `lock-failed: acquire-timeout`. This comes from source reading of both versions and was not run end to end.

**Suggested change:** Do not time out a request while `!hasRealScreen()`: keep it pending and reset only the acquire flags. Alternatively, count `FALLBACK` again and handle focus when a real screen arrives.

### Sleep monitor can miss the resume signal and skip a whole suspend

`wait_until_resume` (`bin/omarchy-system-sleep-monitor`) reads `PreparingForSleep` with `busctl`, then starts a separate `dbus-monitor` to wait for `PrepareForSleep(false)`.

```text
monitor: busctl reads PreparingForSleep = true
         ── user.slice frozen for suspend, then thawed on resume ──
logind:  emits PrepareForSleep(false)          ← before the new subscription exists
monitor: dbus-monitor subscribes, waits for a false that already passed
next suspend: no delay inhibitor held → omarchy-system-sleep-lock never runs
```

**Impact:** When the signal is missed, the loop waits until the next resume. The next suspend (for example menu Suspend, which relies on this monitor to lock) sleeps and resumes unlocked. In systemd v261, `systemd-sleep` freezes `user.slice` and thaws it before logind emits `false`, so the window is reachable. A mocked run of the real script showed the skipped cycle, but the real-world probability was not measured. The merge-base never skipped a whole cycle. Instead, it had no inhibitor for about 2 s after every resume, which this PR closes. The same read-then-subscribe shape exists in `wait_until_idle_awake`.

**Suggested change:** Start the subscription first, then read the property, and act on whichever answer arrives first.

A related minor issue: if SIGTERM arrives between children, `stop()` has no child to kill, and the loop still starts the next `--wait-resume` child. Stopping the service then waits for the stop timeout. This was reproduced in a mocked run. Checking `terminating` immediately before each `run_child` would avoid it.

### Relock rate limit leaves the desktop open

On the fourth involuntary lock loss within 60 s, `onLockLossProbeFinished()` logs `lock-lost: relock-rate-limited` and returns (`Service.qml:238-273`). No timer retries. `lockRequested` stays true, so `isLocked` reports `true` while the session is open, the acquire timeout is not running, and the idle screensaver stays suppressed until an explicit `lock()` call arrives.

**Impact:** The trigger needs repeated compositor lock losses, so this is unlikely, but it is the opposite of the fail-closed goal.

**Suggested change:** Keep retrying with backoff instead of stopping, or clear `lockRequested` and report the failure so status stays truthful.

### Echo-on PAM prompts now leave authentication stuck

`respondToPasswordPrompt()` returns without answering when `passwordPam.responseVisible` is true (`Service.qml:343-350`). Quickshell 0.3.1's PAM subprocess marks echo-on prompts as `responseRequired` and blocks waiting for a reply (`src/services/pam/subprocess.cpp`).

**Impact:** With a PAM stack that issues an echo-on prompt (such as the face-module setup in #8762), the screen stays on "Checking…" with input disabled and no failure or retry. Omarchy's generated `omarchy-lock-password` stack issues no such prompts, so default setups are not affected. The first finding currently masks this, because PAM never starts.

**Suggested change:** Show the prompt so it can be answered, or abort the conversation with a visible failure.

### Smaller notes

- **Lock-failure propagation has no effect:** `consume_sleep_events` returns the lock helper's status, but the `--inhibited)` branch always runs `exit 0`, and the main loop ignores the status. A delay inhibitor also cannot keep the system awake past its timeout (systemd `manager_dispatch_delayed`). Suggested change: drop the propagation and its comment, or state that a failed lock cannot delay suspend.
- **Mask comment:** `LockView.qml:165-167` and `lock-password-mask-test.sh` say Qt shows the real password when the mask glyph is missing. Qt's `QQuickTextInputPrivate::updateDisplayText` fills the display with `passwordCharacter` regardless of glyph coverage, and `passwordMaskDelay: 0` never reveals a character. The `*` change is harmless, but it probably does not address #12727. Suggested change: remove the plaintext claim.
- **Tests and `TMPDIR`:** `lock-focus-after-lid-test.sh` and `lock-auth-failure-test.sh` write to `$TMPDIR` under `set -u`, but neither `test/shell` nor `base-test.sh` defines it. With `TMPDIR` unset, both fail with `TMPDIR: unbound variable`. With it set, they leave `enable-internal.txt`, `respond-fn.txt` and `failure-fn.txt` behind. Suggested change: use a private `mktemp -d` with cleanup, as other tests in the suite do.

**Optional test improvement:** All new tests for `Service.qml` and `LockView.qml` are grep or regex checks, and they pass while password submit is broken. A runtime test that submits a password through `Service` would have caught the first finding. The Qt analog above ran in non-GUI mode without a compositor.

**Verified:**
- A compositor-dropped lock now goes to the fail-closed handler instead of the old wake-and-clear path. `finishUnlock()` clears `lockRequested` before releasing the lock, so authenticated unlocks do not trigger that handler.
- `lock()` no longer returns `"ok"` for a request that never started a lock (#10299). It re-queues and re-arms instead.
- `omarchy-hw-laptop-closed` prefers logind `LidClosed` and falls back to ACPI when logind is unreachable.
- `omarchy-system-secure-if-closed-undocked` locks when the lid is closed with no external display and does not lock when docked.
- The sleep monitor re-arms after resume without restarting the service.
- The bash-based PR tests for these paths (`hw-laptop-closed`, `clamshell-undock-lock`, the resume part of `sleep-monitor`) pass on the head. Against the merge-base with the head tests, 7 of 8 bash tests fail as expected; `lid-close` passes on both because its behavior predates the PR.
- The 30 s blank budget after a deliberate wake is in place.
